title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 93 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 501–504 (Night 93, continuing directly from nights-92), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 93 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Dhāt al-Dawāhī, the Christians' old sorceress, is described in a rhymed portrait of her ugliness, her learning in Islam and her love of the virgin slave-girls; then she puts her plan in motion. Disguised as a Muslim ascetic, shackled, beaten and shut in a chest, she has her men pose as Muslim merchants with a tale of a speaking picture and a holy man imprisoned in a monastery, to draw King Sharrukān into a trap. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ وَالتِّسْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thālithatu wa-al-tisʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the third-and-ninetieth,
sentences.i: And when it was the ninety-third night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَفْرِيدُونَ لَمَّا سَمِعَ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ وَقَعَ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ وَصَارَ أَنْفُهُ تَحْتَ قَدَمَيْهِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-malika afrīdūna lammā samiʿa dhālika al-kalāma waqaʿa maghshiyyan ʿalayhi wa-ṣāra anfuhu taḥta qadamayhi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that King Afrīdūn, when he heard that speech, fell fainted-upon, and his nose became beneath his feet;
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when King Afrīdūn heard these words he fell down in a faint, his nose at his feet.
sentences.n: السعيدان is printed as one word, al-saʿīdu anna, as often. “His nose beneath his feet”: he collapsed in a heap.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ مِنْ غَشْيَتِهِ نَفَضَ الْخَوْفُ جِرَابَ مَعِدَتِهِ فَشَكَا إِلَى الْعَجُوزِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqa min ghashyatihi nafaḍa al-khawfu jirāba maʿidatihi fa-shakā ilā al-ʿajūzi dhāti al-dawāhī
sentences.l: and when he recovered from his faint, the fear shook out the bag of his stomach, and he complained to the old woman, Dhāt al-Dawāhī.
sentences.i: When he came round, terror had turned his stomach inside out, and he poured out his complaint to the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī.
sentences.n: “Fear shook out the sack of his stomach” is a comic image of terror: his insides heaved.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ تِلْكَ اللَّعِينَةُ كَاهِنَةً مِنَ الْكُهَّانِ وَمُتْقِنَةً لِلسِّحْرِ وَالْبُهْتَانِ عَاهِرَةً مَكَّارَةً فَاجِرَةً غَدَّارَةً وَلَهَافَمٌ أَبْخَرُ وَجَفْنٌ أَحْمَرُ وَخَدٌّ أَصْفَرُ بِوَجْهٍ أَغْبَشَ وَطَرْفٍ أَعْمَشَ وَجِسْمٍ أَجْرَبَ وَشَعْرٍ أَشْهَبَ وَظَهْرٍ أَحْدَبَ وَلَوْنٍ حَائِلٍ وَمُخَاطٍ سَائِلٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat tilka al-laʿīnatu kāhinatan mina al-kuhhāni wa-mutqinatan li-al-siḥri wa-al-buhtāni ʿāhiratan makkāratan fājiratan ghaddāratan wa-lahā famun abkharu wa-jafnun aḥmaru wa-khaddun aṣfaru bi-wajhin aghbasha wa-ṭarfin aʿmasha wa-jismin ajraba wa-shaʿrin ashhaba wa-ẓahrin aḥdaba wa-lawnin ḥāʾilin wa-mukhāṭin sāʾilin
sentences.l: And that accursed-one was a soothsayer of the soothsayers, and a master of the sorcery and the slander, a harlot, a wily-one, a wanton, a treacherous-one; and she had a mouth foul-breathed, and an eyelid red, and a cheek yellow, with a face murky, and an eye bleary, and a body mangy, and hair grey, and a back hunched, and a colour faded, and snot running.
sentences.i: Now that accursed woman was a soothsayer among soothsayers, adept in sorcery and lies, a harlot, a schemer, a wanton and a traitor. Her breath stank, her eyelids were red and her cheeks yellow; her face was murky, her eyes bleared, her skin mangy, her hair grey, her back hunched, her colour faded and her nose running.
sentences.n: The print has ولهانم, a misprint for ولهافم (wa-lahā famun, “and she had a mouth”), corrected here; the two words are set solid. The portrait is rhymed prose: kuhhān/buhtān, makkāra/ghaddāra, aghbash/aʿmash, ajrab/ashhab/aḥdab, ḥāʾil/sāʾil. bi- in bi-wajhin: “with”, describing her.

sentences.t: لَكِنَّهَا قَرَأَتْ كُتُبَ الْإِسْلَامِ وَسَافَرَتْ إِلَى بَيْتِ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامِ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ تَطَّلِعَ عَلَى الْأَدْيَانِ وَتَعْرِفَ آيَاتِ الْقُرْآنِ
sentences.tr: lākinnahā qaraʾat kutuba al-islāmi wa-sāfarat ilā bayti allāhi al-ḥarāmi kullu dhālika li-ajli an taṭṭaliʿa ʿalā al-adyāni wa-taʿrifa āyāti al-qurʾāni
sentences.l: But she had read the books of Islam, and travelled to the House of God the Sacred, all that for the sake of that she might look-into the religions and know the verses of the Qurʾān;
sentences.i: Yet she had read the books of Islam and made the journey to God's Sacred House, all so that she might pry into the faiths and learn the verses of the Qurʾān;
sentences.n: The House of God is the Kaʿba at Mecca. Sajʿ: ḥarām/islām, adyān/qurʾān.

sentences.t: وَتَهَوَّدَتْ فِي بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ سَنَتَيْنِ لِتَحُوزَ مَكْرَ الثَّقَلَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-tahawwadat fī bayti al-maqdisi sanatayni li-taḥūza makra al-thaqalayni
sentences.l: and she became-a-Jew in the House of the Holiness two years, that she might gain the guile of the two weighty-ones.
sentences.i: and she lived as a Jew in Jerusalem for two years to master the cunning of men and jinn alike.
sentences.n: Bayt al-Maqdis is Jerusalem. al-thaqalān, “the two weighty ones”, is the Qurʾānic pair of humankind and the jinn.

sentences.t: فَهِيَ آفَةٌ مِنَ الْآفَاتِ وَبَلِيَّةٌ مِنَ الْبَلِيَّاتِ فَاسِدَةُ الِاعْتِقَادِ لَيْسَتْ لِلدِّينِ تَنْقَادُ
sentences.tr: fa-hiya āfatun mina al-āfāti wa-baliyyatun mina al-baliyyāti fāsidatu al-iʿtiqādi laysat li-al-dīni tanqādu
sentences.l: So she was a plague of the plagues and an affliction of the afflictions, corrupt of the belief, not to the religion submitting.
sentences.i: She was a plague among plagues, an affliction among afflictions, rotten in her belief and submissive to no religion.
sentences.n: li-al-dīni, “to religion”, is fronted before its verb for the rhyme: iʿtiqād/tanqād.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَكْثَرُ إِقَامَتِهَا عِنْدَ وَلَدِهَا حَرْدُوبَ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ لِأَجْلِ الْجَوَارِي الْأَبْكَارِ لِأَنَّهَا كَانَتْ تُحِبُّ السِّحَاقَ وَإِنْ تَأَخَّرَ عَنْهَا تَكُونُ فِى انْمِحَاقٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna aktharu iqāmatihā ʿinda waladihā ḥardūba maliki al-rūmi li-ajli al-jawārī al-abkāri li-annahā kānat tuḥibbu al-siḥāqa wa-in taʾakhkhara ʿanhā takūnu fī inmiḥāqin
sentences.l: And the most of her staying was with her son Ḥardūb, king of the Rūm, for the sake of the slave-girls the virgins, because she loved tribadism, and if it was delayed from her she would be in waning.
sentences.i: She spent most of her time with her son Ḥardūb, king of the Rūm, for the sake of the virgin slave-girls; for she loved lying with women, and if she went without it she wasted away.
sentences.n: سحاق (siḥāq, literally “rubbing”) is the classical word for sex between women. Sajʿ: siḥāq/inmiḥāq, the waning of the moon. takūnu, an imperfect after in with a perfect, is looser than Classical.

sentences.t: وَكُلُّ جَارِيَةٍ أَعْجَبَتْهَا تُعَلِّمُهَا الْحِكْمَةَ وَتَسْحَقُ عَلَيْهَا الزَّعْفَرَانَ فَتُغْشَى عَلَيْهَا مِنْ فَرْطِ اللَّذَّةِ مُدَّةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-kullu jāriyatin aʿjabathā tuʿallimuhā al-ḥikmata wa-tasḥaqu ʿalayhā al-zaʿfarāna fa-tughshā ʿalayhā min farṭi al-ladhdhati muddatan mina al-zamāni
sentences.l: And every slave-girl who pleased her, she would teach her the wisdom and grind upon her the saffron, and she would be fainted-upon from excess of the pleasure a space of the time.
sentences.i: Any slave-girl who caught her fancy she would teach philosophy and grind saffron upon, and she would lie swooning a long while from the sheer excess of pleasure.
sentences.n: The print has جاربة, a misprint for جارية (“slave-girl”), corrected here. “Grinding saffron” on someone is a stock euphemism for siḥāq: the verb سحق, “grind, rub”, is the word's own root. Which of the two swoons the Arabic leaves open.

sentences.t: فَمَنْ طَاوَعَتْهَا أَحْسَنَتْ إِلَيْهَا وَرَغَّبَتْ وَلَدَهَا فِيهَا وَمَنْ لَمْ تُطَاوِعْهَا تَتَحَيَّلُ عَلَى هَلَاكِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-man ṭāwaʿathā aḥsanat ilayhā wa-raghghabat waladahā fīhā wa-man lam tuṭāwiʿhā tataḥayyalu ʿalā halākihā
sentences.l: So whoever complied-with her, she did good to her and made her son desirous in her; and whoever did not comply-with her, she would scheme upon her destruction.
sentences.i: A girl who gave in to her she treated kindly and commended to her son's desire; one who would not, she plotted to destroy.

sentences.t: وَسَبَبَ ذَلِكَ عَلِمَتْ مَرْجَانَةُ وَرَيْحَانَةُ وَأُتْرُجَّةُ جَوَارِي أَبْرِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-sababa dhālika ʿalimat marjānatu wa-rayḥānatu wa-utrujjatu jawārī abrīzata
sentences.l: And the cause of that knew Marjāna and Rayḥāna and Utrujja, the slave-girls of Abrīza.
sentences.i: The reason for all this was known to Marjāna, Rayḥāna and Utrujja, Abrīza's slave-girls.
sentences.n: The object, sababa dhālika, is put first for emphasis. Marjāna is “coral”, Rayḥāna “sweet basil”, Utrujja “citron”.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتِ الْمَلِكَةُ أَبْرِيزَةُ تَكْرَهُ الْعَجُوزَ وَتَكْرَهُ أَنْ تَرْقُدَ مَعَهَا لِأَنَّ صُنَانَهَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْ تَحْتِ إِبْطَيْهَا وَرَائِحَةُ فُسَاهَا أَنْتَنُ مِنَ الْجِيفَةِ وَجَسَدُهَا أَخْشَنُ مِنَ اللِّيفَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-kānati al-malikatu abrīzatu takrahu al-ʿajūza wa-takrahu an tarquda maʿahā li-anna ṣunānahā yakhruju min taḥti ibṭayhā wa-rāʾiḥatu fusāhā antanu mina al-jīfati wa-jasaduhā akhshanu mina al-līfati
sentences.l: And Queen Abrīza used to hate the old woman, and hate that she should lie with her, because her armpit-stench came out from under her two armpits, and the smell of her farting was more stinking than the carcass, and her body rougher than the palm-fibre.
sentences.i: Queen Abrīza loathed the old woman and loathed lying with her, for a reek rose from under her armpits, her farts stank worse than carrion, and her body was rougher than palm-fibre.
sentences.n: Sajʿ: jīfa/līfa. The līf is the fibre of the date-palm, used as a scrubber.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ تُرَغِّبُ مَنْ يُسَاحِقُهَا بِالْجَوَاهِرِ وَالتَّعْلِيمِ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat turaghghibu man yusāḥiquhā bi-al-jawāhiri wa-al-taʿlīmi
sentences.l: And she used to entice whoever would rub-with her with the jewels and the teaching,
sentences.i: She would tempt any girl who would lie with her with jewels and lessons,
sentences.n: bi- here is the means: “with” jewels. yusāḥiqu is the verb of siḥāq.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ أَبْرِيزَةُ تَبْرَأُ مِنْهَا إِلَى الْحَكِيمِ الْعَلِيمِ وَلِلَّهِ دَرُّ الْقَائِلِ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat abrīzatu tabraʾu minhā ilā al-ḥakīmi al-ʿalīmi wa-li-allāhi darru al-qāʾili
sentences.l: and Abrīza used to declare-herself-quit of her unto the Wise, the Knowing. And to God (be) the milk of the sayer:
sentences.i: but Abrīza would disown her before God, the Wise, the All-Knowing. How well the poet put it:
sentences.n: li-allāhi darru …, “to God belongs the milk of …”, is the stock phrase of admiration: “how excellent is …!”. Sajʿ: taʿlīm/ʿalīm.

sentences.t:
يَا مَنْ تَسَفَّلَ لِلْغَنِيِّ مَذِلَّةً * وَعَلَى الْفَقِيرِ لَقَدْ عَلَاتَيَّهَا
وَيَزِيْنُ شُمْعَتَهُ بِجَمْعِ دَرَاهِمِ * عَطْرُ الْقَبِيْحَةِ لَابَفِيْ بِفَسَاهَا
sentences.tr:
yā man tasaffala li-al-ghaniyyi madhillatan * wa-ʿalā al-faqīri laqad ʿalā tayyahā
wa-yazīnu shumʿatahu bi-jamʿi darāhimi * ʿiṭru al-qabīḥati lā-bafī bi-fasāhā
sentences.l:
O you who stooped-low to the rich in abasement, and over the poor indeed rose-high … ,
and adorns his candle with the gathering of dirhams: the perfume of the ugly woman does not … for her farting.
sentences.i:
You who grovel before the rich
and lord it over the poor,
you may gild your candle with hoarded coin:
an ugly woman's scent will never cover her farts.
sentences.n: The verse is badly printed and only partly clear. عَلَاتَيَّهَا is perhaps ʿalā tīhuhā, “her arrogance rose high”, and لَابَفِيْ perhaps lā yafī, “is not enough” (ب for ي); both are kept as printed, and the rendering follows those readings. The second line's point is plain: no perfume masks the old woman's stench.

sentences.t: وَنَرْجِعُ إِلَى حَدِيثِ مَكْرِهَا وَدَوَاهِي أَمْرِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-narjiʿu ilā ḥadīthi makrihā wa-dawāhī amrihā
sentences.l: And we return to the tale of her guile and the calamities of her affair.
sentences.i: But let us return to the story of her guile and her calamitous doings.
sentences.n: Sajʿ: makrihā/amrihā, with a play on her name, Dhāt al-Dawāhī.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا سَارَتْ وَسَارَ مَعَهَا عُظَمَاءُ النَّصَارَى وَعَسَاكِرُهُمْ وَتَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى عَسْكَرِ الْإِسْلَامِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā sārat wa-sāra maʿahā ʿuẓamāʾu al-naṣārā wa-ʿasākiruhum wa-tawajjahū ilā ʿaskari al-islāmi
sentences.l: Then she set out, and there set out with her the great-ones of the Christians and their armies, and they made-for the army of Islam.
sentences.i: Then she set out, and the Christian grandees and their troops went with her, heading for the army of Islam.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَهَا دَخَلَ الْمَلِكُ حَرْدُوبُ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ مَالَنَا حَاجَةٌ بِأَمْرِ الْبَطْرِيقِ الْكَبِيرِ وَلَا بِدُعَائِهِ بَلْ نَعْمَلُ بِرَأْىِ أُمِّي ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: wa-baʿdahā dakhala al-maliku ḥardūbu ʿalā al-maliki afrīdūna wa-qāla lahu ayyuhā al-maliku mā lanā ḥājatun bi-amri al-baṭrīqi al-kabīri wa-lā bi-duʿāʾihi bal naʿmalu bi-raʾyi ummī dhāti al-dawāhī
sentences.l: And after her, King Ḥardūb went-in upon King Afrīdūn and said to him: O king, there is not for us need of the affair of the great patriarch nor of his prayer; rather we act by the counsel of my mother, Dhāt al-Dawāhī,
sentences.i: After she had gone, King Ḥardūb came in to King Afrīdūn and said, “O king, we have no need of the great patriarch's business or his prayers; we will act on the counsel of my mother, Dhāt al-Dawāhī,
sentences.n: مالنا is set solid: mā lanā, “we have not”. bi- after ḥāja is “need of”; after naʿmalu, “act on”. The baṭrīq here is the patriarch of the night before.

sentences.t: وَنَنْظُرُ مَا تَعْمَلُ بِخِدَاعِهَا غَيْرِ الْمُتَنَاهِي مَعَ عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَإِنَّهُمْ بِقُوَّتِهِمْ وَاصِلُونَ إِلَيْنَا وَعَنْ قَرِيبٍ يَكُونُونَ لَدَيْنَا وَيُحِيطُونَ بِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-nanẓuru mā taʿmalu bi-khidāʿihā ghayri al-mutanāhī maʿa ʿaskari al-muslimīna fa-innahum bi-quwwatihim wāṣilūna ilaynā wa-ʿan qarībin yakūnūna ladaynā wa-yuḥīṭūna binā
sentences.l: and we see what she does with her deceit, the un-ending, with the army of the Muslims; for they, by their strength, are arriving to us, and before-long they will be with us and surround us.
sentences.i: and see what her endless deceit can do against the Muslim army. For they are coming at us in force; soon they will be upon us and have us surrounded.”
sentences.n: Sajʿ: dawāhī/mutanāhī, ilaynā/ladaynā/binā. bi- in bi-khidāʿihā and bi-quwwatihim is the means: “with, by”; in yuḥīṭūna binā it is what the verb takes, “surround us”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ عَظُمَ فِي قَلْبِهِ الرُّعْبُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku afrīdūnu dhālika al-kalāma ʿaẓuma fī qalbihi al-ruʿbu
sentences.l: And when King Afrīdūn heard that speech, the terror grew-great in his heart,
sentences.i: When King Afrīdūn heard this, the dread in his heart grew great,

sentences.t: فَكَتَبَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ إِلَى سَائِرِأَقَالِيمِ النَّصَارَى يَقُولُ لَهُمْ يَنْبَغِي أَنَّهُ لَا يَتَخَلَّفُ أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمِلَّةِ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ وَالْعِصَابَةِ الصَّلِيبِيَّةِ خُصُوصًا أَهْلَ الْحُصُونِ وَالْقِلَاعِ بَلْ يَأْتُونَ إِلَيْنَا جَمِيعًا رِجَالًا وَرُكْبَانًا وَنِسَاءً وَصِبْيَانًا
sentences.tr: fa-kataba min waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi ilā sāʾiri aqālīmi al-naṣārā yaqūlu lahum yanbaghī annahu lā yatakhallafu aḥadun min ahli al-millati al-naṣrāniyyati wa-al-ʿiṣābati al-ṣalībiyyati khuṣūṣan ahla al-ḥuṣūni wa-al-qilāʿi bal yaʾtūna ilaynā jamīʿan rijālan wa-rukbānan wa-nisāʾan wa-ṣibyānan
sentences.l: and he wrote from his time and his hour to all the regions of the Christians, saying to them: It is fitting that not one should hold-back of the people of the creed, the Christian, and the band, the Cross-ish, especially the people of the forts and the castles; rather let them come to us all together, men-on-foot and riders, and women and boys;
sentences.i: and he wrote at once to every Christian land: “Let no one of the Christian faith and the company of the Cross hang back, least of all the men of the forts and castles; let all come to us, on foot and mounted, women and children too.
sentences.n: سائراقاليم is set solid: sāʾir aqālīm, “all the regions”. yanbaghī annahu lā …, “it is proper that none …”, is looser than Classical yanbaghī an lā. Sajʿ: rijālan/rukbānan … nisāʾan/ṣibyānan.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ عَسْكَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ قَدْ وَطِئُوا أَرْضَنَا فَالْعَجَلَ الْعَجَلَ قَبْلَ حُلُولِ الْوَجَلِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna ʿaskara al-muslimīna qad waṭiʾū arḍanā fa-al-ʿajala al-ʿajala qabla ḥulūli al-wajali
sentences.l: For the army of the Muslims have trodden our land; so the haste, the haste, before the alighting of the dread!
sentences.i: The Muslim army has set foot on our soil. Make haste, make haste, before terror descends!”
sentences.n: ʿaskar, a collective, takes a plural verb. al-ʿajala is accusative of urging: “(make) haste!”. Sajʿ: ʿajal/wajal.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ هَؤُلَاءِ وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْعَجُوزِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي فَإِنَّهَا طَلَعَتْ خَارِجَ الْبَلَدِ مَعَ أَصْحَابِهَا وَأَلْبَسَتْهُمْ زِيَّ تُجَّارِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri hāʾulāʾi wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-ʿajūzi dhāti al-dawāhī fa-innahā ṭalaʿat khārija al-baladi maʿa aṣḥābihā wa-albasathum ziyya tujjāri al-muslimīna
sentences.l: This is what was of the affair of these. And as for what was of the affair of the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, she went-out outside the city with her companions and clothed them in the garb of the merchants of the Muslims.
sentences.i: So much for them. As for the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, she went out of the city with her companions and dressed them as Muslim merchants.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ قَدْ أَخَذَتْ مَعَهَا مِئَةَ بَغْلٍ مُحَمَّلَةً مِنَ الْقُمَاشِ الْأَنْطَاكِيِّ مَا بَيْنَ أَطْلَسٍ مَعْدِنِيٍّ وَدِيبَاجٍ مَلَكِيٍّ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat qad akhadhat maʿahā miʾata baghlin muḥammalatan mina al-qumāshi al-anṭākiyyi mā bayna aṭlasin maʿdiniyyin wa-dībājin malakiyyin wa-ghayri dhālika
sentences.l: And she had taken with her a hundred mules laden with the stuff, the Antiochene, what-is between satin metallic and brocade royal and other-than that.
sentences.i: She had brought along a hundred mules laden with Antioch cloth, satin shot with metal thread, royal brocade and the like.
sentences.n: maʿdinī, “of metal”, is probably satin woven with gold or silver thread.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَتْ مِنَ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ كِتَابًا مَضْمُونُهُ أَنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ التُّجَّارَ مِنْ أَرْضِ الشَّامِ وَكَانُوا فِي دِيَارِنَا فَلَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَتَعَرَّضَ لَهُمْ أَحَدٌ بِسُوءٍ وَلَا يَأْخُذَ مِنْهُمْ عُشْرًا حَتَّى يَصِلُوا إِلَى بِلَادِهِمْ وَمَحَلِّ أَمْنِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhat mina al-maliki afrīdūna kitāban maḍmūnuhu anna hāʾulāʾi al-tujjāra min arḍi al-shāmi wa-kānū fī diyārinā fa-lā yanbaghī an yataʿarraḍa lahum aḥadun bi-sūʾin wa-lā yaʾkhudha minhum ʿushran ḥattā yaṣilū ilā bilādihim wa-maḥalli amnihim
sentences.l: And she took from King Afrīdūn a letter, its content that these merchants are from the land of Syria and were in our lands, so it is not fitting that anyone should interfere with them with evil nor take from them a tenth, until they reach their lands and the place of their safety,
sentences.i: And she had from King Afrīdūn a letter to the effect that these merchants were from Syria and had been staying in his dominions, so that no one was to molest them or take a tithe from them until they reached their own country and safety,
sentences.n: ʿushr, “a tenth”, is the duty levied on merchants' goods. bi-sūʾin, “with evil”: to do them harm.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّ التُّجَّارَ بِهِمْ عَمَارُ الْبِلَادِ وَلَيْسُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْحَرْبِ وَالْفَسَادِ
sentences.tr: li-anna al-tujjāra bihim ʿamāru al-bilādi wa-laysū min ahli al-ḥarbi wa-al-fasādi
sentences.l: because the merchants, by them is the thriving of the lands, and they are not of the people of the war and the corruption.
sentences.i: since it is merchants who make a country prosper, and they are no men of war or mischief.
sentences.n: bihim, “by them”: the merchants are the means by which lands thrive. Sajʿ: bilād/fasād.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلْعُونَةَ ذَاتَ الدَّوَاهِي قَالَتْ لِمَنْ مَعَهَا إِنِّي أُرِيدُأَنْ أُدَبِّرَ حِيلَةً عَلَى هَلَاكِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malʿūnata dhāta al-dawāhī qālat li-man maʿahā innī urīdu an udabbira ḥīlatan ʿalā halāki al-muslimīna
sentences.l: Then the accursed-one, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, said to whoever was with her: I want that I contrive a stratagem upon the destruction of the Muslims.
sentences.i: Then the accursed Dhāt al-Dawāhī said to those with her, “I mean to contrive a trick to destroy the Muslims.”
sentences.n: اريدان is set solid: urīdu an.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهَا أَيَّتُهَا الْمَلِكَةُ مُرِينَا بِمَا شِئْتِ فَنَحْنُ تَحْتَ طَاعَتِكِ فَلَا أَحْبَطَ الْمَسِيحُ عَمَلَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahā ayyatuhā al-malikatu murīnā bi-mā shiʾti fa-naḥnu taḥta ṭāʿatiki fa-lā aḥbaṭa al-masīḥu ʿamalaki
sentences.l: And they said to her: O queen, command us with what you wish, for we are under your obedience; and may the Messiah not bring-to-nothing your work.
sentences.i: They answered, “O queen, command us as you will, for we are yours to obey; may the Messiah never let your work come to nothing.”
sentences.n: The print has مربنا, a misprint for مرينا (murīnā, “command us”, the feminine imperative), corrected here. With amara, bi- names the thing commanded. lā with the perfect is a wish.

sentences.t: فَلَبِسَتْ ثِيَابًا مِنَ الصُّوفِ الْأَبْيَضِ النَّاعِمِ وَحَكَّتْ جَبِينَهَا حَتَّى صَارَلَهُ وَسْمٌ عَظِيمٌ وَدَهَنَتْهُ بِدِهَانٍ دَبَّرَتْهُ حَتَّى صَارَلَهُ ضَوْوٌ عَظِيمٌ
sentences.tr: fa-labisat thiyāban mina al-ṣūfi al-abyaḍi al-nāʿimi wa-ḥakkat jabīnahā ḥattā ṣāra lahu wasmun ʿaẓīmun wa-dahanathu bi-dihānin dabbarathu ḥattā ṣāra lahu ḍawʾun ʿaẓīmun
sentences.l: And she put on clothes of the wool, the white, the soft, and rubbed her forehead until there became to it a great brand, and anointed it with an ointment she had contrived until there became to it a great shining.
sentences.i: So she put on robes of soft white wool and rubbed her forehead until it bore a great mark, then anointed it with an ointment of her own devising until it shone brightly.
sentences.n: Wool (ṣūf) is the dress of ascetics, and the mark on the brow is the callus of constant prostration: she is making herself look like a Muslim holy woman. صارله is set solid both times (ṣāra lahu). ضوو is the print's spelling of ضوء, “light, sheen”, the hamza written as a second wāw; it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتِ الْمَلْعُونَهُ نَحِيلَةَ الْجِسْمِ غَائِرَةَ الْعَيْنَيْنِ فَقَيَّدَتْ رِجْلَيْهَا مِنْ فَوْقِ قَدَمَيْهَا وَسَارَتْ حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ إِلَى عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-kānati al-malʿūnatu naḥīlata al-jismi ghāʾirata al-ʿaynayni fa-qayyadat rijlayhā min fawqi qadamayhā wa-sārat ḥattā waṣalat ilā ʿaskari al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And the accursed-one was thin of the body, sunken of the two eyes; and she fettered her legs from above her feet, and went until she reached the army of the Muslims.
sentences.i: The accursed woman was lean of body and hollow-eyed. She shackled her legs above the feet and went on until she reached the Muslim army.
sentences.n: الملعونه ends in hāʾ for tāʾ marbūṭa, the edition's frequent spelling.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَلَّتِ الْقَيْدَ مِنْ رِجْلَيْهَا وَقَدْ أَثَّرَ الْقَيْدُ فِي سَاقَيْهَا ثُمَّ دَهَنَتْهَا بِدَمِ الْأَخَوَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥallati al-qayda min rijlayhā wa-qad aththara al-qaydu fī sāqayhā thumma dahanathā bi-dami al-akhawayni
sentences.l: Then she loosed the fetter from her legs, and the fetter had left-a-mark in her shanks; then she smeared them with the blood of the two brothers,
sentences.i: Then she took the shackle off her legs, which had left its marks on her shins, and smeared them with dragon's blood,
sentences.n: Dam al-akhawayn, “the blood of the two brothers”, is dragon's blood, a dark red resin; here it fakes wounds.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَتْ مَنْ مَعَهَا أَنْ يَضْرِبُوهَا ضَرْبًا عَنِيفًا وَأَنْ يَضَعُوهَا فِي صُنْدُوقٍ وَأَعْلِنُوا فِي كَلِمَةِ التَّوْحِيدِ وَمَا عَلَيْكُمْ فِي ذَلِكَ مِنْ بَاسٍ شَدِيدٍ
sentences.tr: wa-amarat man maʿahā an yaḍribūhā ḍarban ʿanīfan wa-an yaḍaʿūhā fī ṣundūqin wa-aʿlinū fī kalimati al-tawḥīdi wa-mā ʿalaykum fī dhālika min bāsin shadīdin
sentences.l: and she ordered whoever was with her that they beat her a beating violent, and that they put her in a chest: “And proclaim in the word of the Oneness, and there is not upon you in that any harm severe.”
sentences.i: and she ordered her companions to beat her hard and put her in a chest. “And declare God's oneness aloud,” she said; “there is no great harm for you in that.”
sentences.n: The sentence slides from report into her own words. Kalimat al-tawḥīd is the Muslim profession of faith: she tells her Christians to pass as Muslims. باس is بأس, “harm”, without its hamza. Sajʿ: tawḥīd/shadīd.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهَا كَيْفَ نَضْرِبُكِ وَأَنْتِ سَيِّدَتُنَا ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي أُمُّ الْمَلِكِ الْمُبَاهِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahā kayfa naḍribuki wa-anti sayyidatunā dhātu al-dawāhī ummu al-maliki al-mubāhī
sentences.l: And they said to her: How shall we beat you, and you are our lady Dhāt al-Dawāhī, mother of the king, the vaunting?
sentences.i: They said, “How can we beat you, our lady Dhāt al-Dawāhī, mother of the glorious king?”
sentences.n: mubāhī, “vying in glory”, rhymes with dawāhī.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَا لَوْمَ وَلَا تَعْنِيفَ عَلَى مَنْ يَأْتِي الْكَنِيفَ وَلِأَجْلِ الضَّرُورَاتِ تُبَاحُ الْمَحْظُورَاتُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lā lawma wa-lā taʿnīfa ʿalā man yaʾtī al-kanīfa wa-li-ajli al-ḍarūrāti tubāḥu al-maḥẓūrātu
sentences.l: And she said: No blame and no reproach upon who comes to the privy; and for the sake of the necessities the forbidden-things are permitted.
sentences.i: She said, “No one blames or scolds a person for going to the privy, and necessity makes the forbidden lawful.
sentences.n: Two sayings. The first excuses what must be done, however low; the second is a maxim of Islamic law, here in a Christian's mouth. Sajʿ: taʿnīf/kanīf, ḍarūrāt/maḥẓūrāt.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ أَنْ تَضَعُونِي فِى الصُّنْدُوقِ خُذُوهُ فِي جُمْلَةِ الْأَمْوَالِ وَاحْمِلُوهُ عَلَى الْبِغَالِ وَمُرُّوا بِذَلِكَ بَيْنَ عَسْكَرِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَلَا تَخْشَوْا شَيًا مِنَ الْمَلَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda an taḍaʿūnī fī al-ṣundūqi khudhūhu fī jumlati al-amwāli wa-iḥmilūhu ʿalā al-bighāli wa-murrū bi-dhālika bayna ʿaskari al-islāmi wa-lā takhshaw shayan mina al-malāmi
sentences.l: And after that you put me in the chest, take it in the sum of the goods, and load it on the mules, and pass with that among the army of Islam, and do not fear a thing of the blame.
sentences.i: Once you have put me in the chest, take it along with the rest of the goods, load it on the mules and pass with it through the army of Islam, and fear no reproach.
sentences.n: murrū bi-dhālika: with marra, bi- is what one takes along, “pass with it”. شيا is the edition's spelling of شيئا. Sajʿ: amwāl/bighāl, islām/malām.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ تَعَرَّضَ لَكُمْ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَسَلِّمُوا لَهُ الْبِغَالَ وَمَا عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ وَانْصَرِفُوا إِلَى مَلِكِهِمْ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَاسْتَغِيثُوا بِهِ وَقُولُوا
sentences.tr: wa-in taʿarraḍa lakum aḥadun mina al-muslimīna fa-sallimū lahu al-bighāla wa-mā ʿalayhā mina al-amwāli wa-inṣarifū ilā malikihim ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-istaghīthū bihi wa-qūlū
sentences.l: And if anyone of the Muslims interferes with you, hand-over to him the mules and what is on them of the goods, and betake-yourselves to their king Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and cry-for-help to him, and say:
sentences.i: If any Muslim stops you, hand over to him the mules and the goods they carry, then go to their king, Ḍawʾ al-Makān, appeal to him, and say:
sentences.n: istaghātha bi-: “call on (someone) for help”.

sentences.t: نَحْنُ كُنَّا فِي بِلَادِ الْكَفَرَةِ وَلَمْ يَأْخُذُوا مِنَّا شَيْأً بَلْ كَتَبُوا لَنَا تَوْقِيعًا أَنَّهُ لَا يَتَعَرَّضُ لَنَا أَحَدٌ فَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَ أَنْتُمْ أَمْوَالَنَا
sentences.tr: naḥnu kunnā fī bilādi al-kafarati wa-lam yaʾkhudhū minnā shayʾan bal katabū lanā tawqīʿan annahu lā yataʿarraḍu lanā aḥadun fa-kayfa taʾkhudhūna antum amwālanā
sentences.l: We were in the lands of the unbelievers, and they did not take from us a thing; rather they wrote for us a warrant that no one should interfere with us; so how do you take, you, our goods?
sentences.i: ‘We were in the land of the infidels, and they took nothing from us; they even wrote us a warrant that no one should molest us. How then can you take our goods?
sentences.n: شيأ is the edition's spelling of شيئا.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا كِتَابُ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ الَّذِي مَضْمُونُهُ أَنْ لَا يَتَعَرَّضَ لَنَا أَحَدٌ بِمَكْرُوهٍ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā kitābu maliki al-rūmi alladhī maḍmūnuhu an lā yataʿarraḍa lanā aḥadun bi-makrūhin
sentences.l: And this is the letter of the king of the Rūm, whose content is that no one should interfere with us with a hateful-thing.
sentences.i: Here is the letter of the king of the Rūm, which says that no one is to do us any harm.’

sentences.t: فَإِذَا قَالَ وَمَا الَّذِي رَبِحْتُمُوهُ مِنْ بِلَادِ الرُّومِ فِي تِجَارَتِكُمْ فَقُولُوا لَهُ رَبِحْنَا خَلَاصَ رَجُلٍ زَاهِدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā qāla wa-mā alladhī rabiḥtumūhu min bilādi al-rūmi fī tijāratikum fa-qūlū lahu rabiḥnā khalāṣa rajulin zāhidin
sentences.l: And if he says: And what is it that you gained from the lands of the Rūm in your trading? then say to him: We gained the deliverance of a man ascetic,
sentences.i: And if he asks, ‘What profit did you make in the land of the Rūm from your trading?’, tell him, ‘Our profit was the rescue of a holy ascetic,

sentences.t: وَقَدْ كَانَ فِي سِرْدَابٍ تَحْتَ الْأَرْضِ لَهُ فِيهِ نَحْوُ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ عَامًا وَهُوَ يَسْتَغِيثُ فَلَا يُغَاثُ بَلْ يُعَذِّبُهُ الْكُفَّارُ لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا
sentences.tr: wa-qad kāna fī sirdābin taḥta al-arḍi lahu fīhi naḥwu khamsata ʿashara ʿāman wa-huwa yastaghīthu fa-lā yughāthu bal yuʿadhdhibuhu al-kuffāru laylan wa-nahāran
sentences.l: and he had been in a vault under the earth, to him in it about fifteen years, and he crying-for-help and not being helped; rather the unbelievers tormented him night and day.
sentences.i: who had lain in an underground vault for some fifteen years, crying for help and never helped, while the unbelievers tortured him night and day.
sentences.n: lahu fīhi naḥwu …, “to him in it about …”: the usual way of saying how long someone has been somewhere.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَنَا عِلْمٌ بِذَلِكَ مَعَ أَنَّنَا أَقَمْنَا فِى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ مُدَّةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ وَبِعْنَا بَضَائِعَنَا وَاشْتَرَيْنَا خِلَافَهَا وَجَهَّزْنَا حَالَنَا وَعَزَمْنَا عَلَى الرَّحِيلِ إِلَى بِلَادِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-lam yakun ʿindanā ʿilmun bi-dhālika maʿa annanā aqamnā fī al-qusṭanṭīniyyati muddatan mina al-zamāni wa-biʿnā baḍāʾiʿanā wa-ishtaraynā khilāfahā wa-jahhaznā ḥālanā wa-ʿazamnā ʿalā al-raḥīli ilā bilādinā
sentences.l: And there was not with us knowledge of that, although we had stayed in Constantinople a space of the time, and sold our wares and bought other-than-them, and made-ready our state, and resolved upon the departure to our lands.
sentences.i: We knew nothing of it, though we had stayed in Constantinople a good while, sold our wares and bought others, made our preparations and resolved to leave for home.
sentences.n: The print has بصائعنا, a misprint for بضائعنا (“our wares”), corrected here.

sentences.t: وَبِتْنَا تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ نَتَحَدَّثُ فِي أَمْرِ السَّفَرِ فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحْنَا رَأَيْنَا صُورَةً مُصَوَّرَةً فِى الْحَائِطِ
sentences.tr: wa-bitnā tilka al-laylata nataḥaddathu fī amri al-safari fa-lammā aṣbaḥnā raʾaynā ṣūratan muṣawwaratan fī al-ḥāʾiṭi
sentences.l: And we passed-the-night that night talking in the matter of the journey; and when we came-to-morning, we saw an image imaged on the wall.
sentences.i: That night we sat up talking over the journey, and in the morning we saw a picture painted on the wall.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرُبْنَا مِنْهَا تَأَمَّلْنَاهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ تَحَرَّكَتْ وَقَالَتْ يَا مُسْلِمُونَ هَلْ فِيكُمْ مَنْ يُعَامِلُ رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qarubnā minhā taʾammalnāhā fa-idhā hiya taḥarrakat wa-qālat yā muslimūna hal fīkum man yuʿāmilu rabba al-ʿālamīna
sentences.l: And when we drew-near to it we gazed-at it, and behold, it moved and said: O Muslims, is there among you one who deals with the Lord of the Worlds?
sentences.i: When we came close and looked at it, behold, it moved and said, “O Muslims, is there one among you who will do business with the Lord of the Worlds?”
sentences.n: yuʿāmilu, “deal, trade with”: a merchant's word turned to piety, a deed whose return comes from God.

sentences.t: فَقُلْنَا وَكَيْفَ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَتْ تِلْكَ الصُّورَةُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْطَقَنِي لَكُمْ لِيُقَوِّيَ يَقِينَكُمْ وَيَهُمَّكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَتَخْرُجُوا مِنْ بِلَادِ الْكَافِرِينَ وَتَقْصِدُوا عَسْكَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-qulnā wa-kayfa dhālika fa-qālat tilka al-ṣūratu inna allāha anṭaqanī lakum li-yuqawwiya yaqīnakum wa-yahummakum dīnukum wa-takhrujū min bilādi al-kāfirīna wa-taqṣidū ʿaskara al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And we said: And how is that? And that image said: God has made-me-speak to you, to strengthen your certainty, and (that) your religion concern you, and (that) you go out from the lands of the unbelievers and make-for the army of the Muslims;
sentences.i: We said, “How so?”, and the picture said, “God has given me speech for your sake, to strengthen your faith and make your religion your care, so that you leave the land of the unbelievers and go to the army of the Muslims.
sentences.n: ويهمكم is read wa-yahummakum dīnukum, “and that your religion may weigh with you”; the sense is not quite certain. li- in li-yuqawwiya is “so that”, and governs the verbs that follow.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ فِيهِمْ سَيْفَ الرَّحْمٰنِ وَبَطَلَ الزَّمَانِ الْمَلِكَ شَرْكَانَ وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُفْتَحُ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةُ بِهِ وَيَمْلِكُ أَهْلَ الْمِلَّةِ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna fīhim sayfa al-raḥmāni wa-baṭala al-zamāni al-malika sharrukāna wa-huwa alladhī yuftaḥu al-qusṭanṭīniyyatu bihi wa-yamliku ahla al-millati al-naṣrāniyyati
sentences.l: For among them is the sword of the Merciful and the hero of the age, King Sharrukān, and he is the one who Constantinople will be opened by him, and he will possess the people of the creed, the Christian.
sentences.i: For among them is the Sword of the Merciful, the champion of the age, King Sharrukān: it is by his hand that Constantinople will be taken, and he will rule the people of the Christian faith.
sentences.n: yuftaḥu … bihi, “will be opened by him”: fataḥa, “open”, is the word for conquering a city.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا قَطَعْتُمْ سَفَرَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ تَجِدُوا دَيْرًا يُعْرَفُ بِدَيْرِ مَطَرْ وَحَنَّى وَفِيهِ صَوْمَعَةٌ فَاقْصِدُوهَا بِصِدْقِ نِيَّتِكُمْ وَتَحَيَّلُوا عَلَى الْوُصُولِ إِلَيْهَا بِقُوَّةِ عَزِيمَتِكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā qaṭaʿtum safara thalāthati ayyāmin tajidū dayran yuʿrafu bi-dayri maṭar wa-ḥannā wa-fīhi ṣawmaʿatun fa-iqṣidūhā bi-ṣidqi niyyatikum wa-taḥayyalū ʿalā al-wuṣūli ilayhā bi-quwwati ʿazīmatikum
sentences.l: So when you have cut a journey of three days, you find a monastery known by the Monastery of Maṭar wa-Ḥannā, and in it a hermit's-cell; so make-for it with the truth of your intention, and use-stratagem upon the reaching to it with the strength of your resolve,
sentences.i: When you have gone three days' journey you will find a monastery called the Monastery of Maṭar wa-Ḥannā, with a hermit's cell in it. Make for it in good faith, and by strong resolve find some means of reaching it,
sentences.n: tajidū without its final nūn after fa-idhā is Middle Arabic (Classical tajidūna). The monastery's name is printed as two words, مطر وحنى, and is given as printed. bi- after yuʿrafu: “known by (the name)”; in bi-ṣidqi and bi-quwwati, “with”. Sajʿ: niyyatikum/ʿazīmatikum.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّ فِيهَا رَجُلًا عَابِدًا مِنْ بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ اسْمُهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَهُوَ مِنْ أَدْيَنِ النَّاسِ وَلَهُ كَرَامَاتٌ تُزِيحُ الشَّكَّ وَالْإِلْبَاسَ
sentences.tr: li-anna fīhā rajulan ʿābidan min bayti al-maqdisi ismuhu ʿabdu allāhi wa-huwa min adyani al-nāsi wa-lahu karāmātun tuzīḥu al-shakka wa-al-ilbāsa
sentences.l: because in it is a man, a worshipper, from the House of the Holiness, his name ʿAbd Allāh, and he is of the most-religious of the people, and he has wonders that remove the doubt and the confusion.
sentences.i: for in it is a devout man from Jerusalem named ʿAbd Allāh, one of the most pious of men, whose miracles dispel all doubt and confusion.
sentences.n: karāmāt are the wonders worked by saints, as distinct from the miracles of prophets. Sajʿ: nās/ilbās.

sentences.t: قَدْ خَدَعَهُ بَعْضُ الرُّهْبَانِ وَسَجَنَهُ فِي سِرْدَابٍ لَهُ فِيهِ مُدَّةٌ مَدِيدَةٌ مِنَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: qad khadaʿahu baʿḍu al-ruhbāni wa-sajanahu fī sirdābin lahu fīhi muddatun madīdatun mina al-zamāni
sentences.l: Some-one of the monks has deceived him and imprisoned him in a vault, to him in it a span extended of the time.
sentences.i: A certain monk tricked him and shut him in a vault, where he has been for a long, long time.
sentences.n: Sajʿ: ruhbān/zamān.

sentences.t: وَفِي إِنْقَاذِهِ إِرْضَاءُ رَبِّ الْعِبَادِ لِأَنَّ فَكَاكَهُ مِنْ أَفْضَلِ الْجِهَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī inqādhihi irḍāʾu rabbi al-ʿibādi li-anna fakākahu min afḍali al-jihādi
sentences.l: And in his rescue is the pleasing of the Lord of the servants, because his release is of the most-excellent of the holy-war.
sentences.i: To rescue him is to please the Lord of His servants, for freeing him is among the noblest kinds of holy war.”
sentences.n: Sajʿ: ʿibād/jihād.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعَجُوزَ لَمَّا اتَّفَقَتْ مَعَ مَنْ مَعَهَا عَلَى هَذَا الْكَلَامِ قَالَتْ فَإِذَا أَلْقَى إِلَيْكُمْ سَمْعَهُ الْمَلِكُ شَرْكَانُ فَقُولُوا لَهُ فَلَمَّا سَمِعْنَا هَذَا الْكَلَامَ مِنْ تِلْكَ الصُّورَةِ عَلِمْنَا أَنَّ ذَلِكَ الْعَابِدَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿajūza lammā ittafaqat maʿa man maʿahā ʿalā hādhā al-kalāmi qālat fa-idhā alqā ilaykum samʿahu al-maliku sharrukānu fa-qūlū lahu fa-lammā samiʿnā hādhā al-kalāma min tilka al-ṣūrati ʿalimnā anna dhālika al-ʿābida …
sentences.l: Then the old woman, when she had agreed with whoever was with her upon this speech, said: And when King Sharrukān casts his hearing to you, say to him: And when we heard this speech from that image, we knew that that worshipper …
sentences.i: When the old woman had settled all this with her companions, she said, “And when King Sharrukān gives you his ear, say to him: ‘When we heard these words from the picture, we knew that this holy man …’”
sentences.n: alqā ilaykum samʿahu, “cast his hearing to you”: listened closely. The old woman's instructions break off as morning comes; the next night takes them up.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as in every night.
